text:
Aisha: Heads-up — noticed a ~12% uptick in GPU preemptions in us-west-2 this morning. Low-priority pools got hit and ~7% of requests flapped into fallback paths. Need a short routing plan to avoid customer errors.
Ryan: saw that. Any scheduled maintenance? logs show a bunch of reclaim events 03:12–03:28 UTC.
Mari: not maintenance. Cloud price spike + autoscaler churn. We're seeing short-lived 20–30s backpressure bursts on the preemptible pools.
Tony: rough idea: implement a short-lived "splice" fallback that prefers same-region reserved capacity, then a smaller quantized model-variant, then cross-region. Keep cross-region as last resort. Also restrict reserved promotion to paid tiers.
Aisha: yep — important: no silent promotion of free-tier to reserved. We should also minimize cold-starts when switching models.
Ryan: draft policy (pseudo-yaml):
```
fallback_policy:
  on_preemptible_eviction:
    - step: route_to_reserved_same_region
      allowed_tiers: ["enterprise", "dedicated"]
      max_reroute_ms: 100
    - step: route_to_model_variant
      variant: "quant_small"
      allowed_tiers: ["all"]
      max_reroute_ms: 10000
      soft_degrade: true
    - step: cross_region_failover
      target_regions: ["us-east-1", "ap-northeast-1"]
      circuit_breaker_threshold: 0.6
```
Mari: quick numbers from today's incident: when fallback -> quant_small we saw p50 +6ms, p95 +40ms, p99 +120ms for small workloads; cost saved ~9% vs immediate reserved failover. Cross-region adds ~50–120ms depending on region.
Tony: ran a simulator with current traffic mix: using variant-first reduces reserve promotion by 78% and lowers expected monthly spend on reserved spills by ~18%, but enterprise p99 goes up ~1.8ms (still within SLA).
Aisha: tradeoffs sound reasonable. Action items: (1) implement policy in routing service as config toggle, (2) canary at 5% traffic for 2h, (3) add automated rollback if error-rate + latency budget breached.
infra-bot: [alert] us-west-2 preemptible reclaim spike detected — 1747008800 — spikes: 12% evictions / 10m
Ryan: for canary, we need metrics: per-tier error-rate, p99 latency, token-cost delta, and reserve-promotion count. Also add a probe that verifies KV cache reuse when switching model variants.
Mari: I'll wire the dashboard panels, link will be in #monitoring once ready. Also adding a synthetic workload that simulates 25% short-lived sessions to test churn paths.
Tony: one more thing — consider a short TTL local shard that caches model-weights for the quant_small variant to avoid extra cold starts on fallback.
Aisha: agreed. Let's run canary tomorrow 10:00 UTC. @Ryan please own rollout; @Mari add dashboards; @Tony prototype cache-ttl. We'll reconvene after 2h canary.
